An asymptomatic 34-year-old woman with a history of myopic soft contact lens wear was referred to ophthalmology for evaluation of bilateral corneal clouding refractory to a contact lens holiday and a short course of topical corticosteroids.
Slit-lamp examination revealed fine, grayish-white deposits throughout all layers of the corneal stroma.
Testing revealed hemoglobin of 10.8 (normal 11.5 to 15.5) g/dl with stomatocytes, normal serum creatinine, and urine protein of 30 mg/dl with no bacteria.
| HDL | <10 mg/dl |
Her past medical history was remarkable for obesity, mild anemia, and “low cholesterol.”

phenotype_specificity.statement: Proband 3 (34256778): FLD phenotype with corneal opacities, very low HDL-C, anemia, glomerulopathy and very low LCAT activity; no testing of other genes is reported. Case report (34316822): corneal clouding, HDL <10 mg/dl, anemia and proteinuria; a panel of ABCA1, APOA1 and LCAT was sequenced and only the LCAT variant is reported, and the authors list Tangier disease and apoA1 deficiency in the differential.

quotes.quote: She had an FLD phenotype with extremely low levels of HDL-C, anemia and kidney disease (glomerulopathy).There was no clinical or biochemical evidence of FLD or FED in her parents or sibling.
The proband had extremely low LCAT activity (7.3 nmol/mL/hr, LCAT specific activity in control 145.34nmol/mL/hr) and a 60 % reduction in PON-1 activity compared with controls.
She had attended consultations with several specialists, had undergone three kidney biopsies and one bone marrow aspiration; despite this she had not been diagnosed.
Genetic testing via Gene DX Xome Slice, sequencing ABCA1, APOA1, and LCAT, was positive for LCAT c.490 C>T (p.R164C) as the likely pathogenic variant, confirming the diagnosis of LCAT deficiency.

However, other primary (monogenic) causes of extremely low HDL levels that may also present with diffuse corneal opacification include fish-eye disease, Tangier disease, and apolipoprotein A1 (apoA1) deficiency, all disorders of the lecithin cholesterol acyl transferase (LCAT) system.
Testing revealed hemoglobin of 10.8 (normal 11.5 to 15.5) g/dl with stomatocytes, normal serum creatinine, and urine protein of 30 mg/dl with no bacteria.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: missense, p.(Arg164Cys); 34316822 states p.R164C. The papers describe LCAT deficiency as autosomal recessive due to loss of LCAT function; 34256778 says the Arg140 domain is crucial for activity (but that refers to the Arg140His change in its case description).

quotes.quote: In this patient, the 490th base of LCAT (c.490) was subject to a C>T mutation. Thus, the 164th amino acid in the protein’s primary structure was a cysteine rather than an arginine (p.R.164 C).
LCAT deficiency is a rare (incidence < 1:1,000,000) autosomal recessive disorder resulting from a mutation of the LCAT gene.
Patients with complete loss of LCAT function are designated as having LCAT deficiency.
LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.
This domain (where Arg140 resides) is crucial for an enzymatically active LCAT protein, mutations in this region possibly affect tertiary structure.

authors_classification.statement: 34316822 calls c.490 C>T (p.R164C) 'the likely pathogenic variant'; criteria not stated. 34256778 gives no classification for proband 3's variant.

concerns: 34256778 contradicts itself for proband 3: the results text and Table 3 give c.490 C > T (which predicts Arg164Cys), but the case description says 'a G to A substitution on codon 140 converting Arginine to Histidine', and the discussion links it to the Austrian Arg140His kindred (reference [39]). Arg140His in mature-protein numbering would correspond to c.491G>A rather than c.490C>T. The panel should not count proband 3 for c.490C>T without resolving this.

Legacy (mature-protein) numbering in 34256778 (codon 140) vs full-length numbering in 34316822 (p.R164C); the 24-residue difference is consistent with the signal peptide but is not stated by either paper.
34316822 reports only one LCAT variant in a recessive disease and does not state zygosity; the Xome Slice panel may not detect a second allele such as a large deletion (not discussed by the authors).
Table 1 of 34256778 also lists c.490 C > T in the Japanese row (21 cases, cohort-level); that carrier cannot be attributed to a person from this paper and is not counted here.
The two identities (Mexican woman aged 29 from Monterrey; US case-report woman aged 34, adopted) show no sign of being the same person.
notes_for_panel: Main issue: the review's own case description for proband 3 describes Arg140His (G to A), not c.490C>T (Arg164Cys); only the 34316822 patient clearly carries c.490C>T, with zygosity unreported. Transcript in 34256778 is NM_000229.1.
